newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus eyes Alenia, Northrop as 3XX partners.
newsitem.headline: Airbus eyes Alenia, Northrop as 3XX partners.

text.p: European plane consortium Airbus Industrie has held talks with Italy's Alenia and U.S. giant Northrop Grumman as potential partners for its A3XX large plane project, an Airbus spokesman said.

Airbus is looking for partners outside the four-member partnership to provide up to 40 percent of the estimated $8 billion needed to develop the 555-seater A3XX. The plane would compete with derivatives of Boeing's 747 jumbo jet.
Talks aimed at bringing Airbus into a planned 100-seater jet to be built in China with the European AIA consortium led Airbus to discuss the large plane with Alenia, the spokesman said.
Alenia, a unit of Finmeccanica, is a member of Aero International Asia (AIA), along with Airbus partners SNI Aerospatiale and British Aerospace Plc.
"Overall talks on the 100-seater involved a number of other side issues and included industrial participation in the A3XX," the spokesman said.
He added that Airbus had been discussing the A3XX product with Northrop Grumman but declined to give further details.
Northrop Grumman is a major U.S. defence contractor building the JSTARS ground surveillance plane.
Airbus has said it is looking in Russia, southeast Asia and the United States for potential A3XX partners to share the risk finance.
Manfred Bischoff, chairman of Airbus partner Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa), said on August 30 he was trying to bring Alenia and Sweden's Saab into a future autonomous Airbus company.
Saab chairman Benght Halse has said the Swedish company wanted to be involved in the A3XX project but for the time being excluded co-operation on smaller planes.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
